facts.claim: Emily Post Institute: "Utensils are placed in the order of use; from the outside in."
Emily Post Institute: "Forks go to the left of the plate, and knives and spoons go to the right." It adds that the oyster fork is the only fork placed to the right of the setting if it will be used.
Emily Post Institute: "Finally, only set the table with utensils you will use."

Emily Post Institute (basic setting): to the right of the plate is "the knife (blade facing inward toward the fork and plate)"; "The water glass is placed above the knife or at 45-degree angle to the right of the knife."

Emily Post Institute: dessert utensils "can be brought out with dessert or set above the setting during the entire meal. If set for the entire meal, the fork is placed so the handle points toward the left, and the spoon sits above the fork with its handle facing to the right." Formal: "For the most traditional and formal of settings, the dessert spoon is placed above the dessert fork."

Emily Post Institute: wine glasses, "one (maybe two)" in an informal/semi-formal setting, are "placed to the right of the water glass"; in a formal setting a different wine for every course "would result in a cascade of glasses flowing to the right of the setting."

Emily Post Institute: "The butter knife is placed on the butter plate with the blade facing inward toward the diner", handle pointing to the right for right-handed diners. (The page text does not state which side the butter plate sits on; that appears only in its diagrams.)

Emily Post Institute (formal): "A charger plate may be used (or not). The napkin might be set to the left or placed in the center of the charger." On the fork-on-napkin question: "At Emily Post, we say it's really up to you and your style."

Emily Post Institute: when clearing for dessert, "remove the unused utensils (except the dessert utensils if they are out) as well as the butter plate and butter knife." Finger bowls, if used, "are brought out after a messy course instead of being placed at the setting the entire meal."

insider_details.detail: Ask the caterer for the final menu before the place setting is locked: the setting is built from the menu (outside-in, one utensil per course, nothing that won't be used), so a late soup or sorbet course changes every place at every table.

If dessert cutlery is set above the plate from the start, it frees the waitstaff from a cutlery run at dessert, which matters at a long-table reception where service has to be quick; the traditional order is spoon above fork.

A drinks package with several wines means a cascade of glasses to the right of the water glass; check the table width can take it alongside centrepieces and candles before choosing a low, wide arrangement.

Napkin placement is a styling choice, not a rule: to the left or centred on the charger are both correct, which is why a folded napkin with a name card on the charger is the easy place to bring in a theme.
